extracted.intended_audience: general educated readers, students of history/political theory, and advocates/planners of international organization
extracted.subtask_description: An outline of the forces, requirements, and institutional characteristics by which humanity might be unified into a federal world state; addresses moral, educational, religious, economic, scientific, and political preconditions and outcomes. Useful for assessing proposals for world government or evaluating historical arguments for international organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-war mental awakening / destruction of fixed ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: There has been 'a destruction of fixed ideas, prejudices, and mental limitations' during the Great War years, producing a universal awakening and greater readiness for collective ideas and action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wells argues that 'never before can there have been so great and so universal an awakening from assumed and accepted things' and that millions are now 'open to fresh ideas of association and duty and relationship as they were never open before.' This mental readiness is presented as a necessary precondition for large-scale political change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political education as the supreme task
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'supreme task before men at the present time is political education' — preparing minds for world coöperation by teaching a common interpretation of history and purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wells emphasizes educational work 'by pen and persuasion, in schools and colleges and books, and in the highways and byways of public life.' He criticizes the League for not communicating to common men and stresses that minds must be prepared by 'experience and knowledge and thought.'

rubrics_metrics.name: A common interpretation / new telling of history
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocates must produce 'a new telling and interpretation, a common interpretation, of history' to prepare minds everywhere for world coöperation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as the very essence of the educational task: to bring to the minds of all men, as a necessary basis for world coöperation, a shared historical narrative that supports unity rather than nationalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merge sovereignty / subordinate nationality (world league of men)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sovereignty must be merged and nationality subordinated; the world needs not a mere league of nations but 'a world league of men' in which national sovereignty is subordinated to broader human interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wells critiques the 1919 League of Nations as 'a mere partial league of governments' that 'emphasizes nationality; it defers to sovereignty.' He holds that the world perishes unless sovereignty is merged and nationality subordinated—an explicit political standard for evaluating federative proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increasing destructiveness of modern war
rubrics_metrics.description: The growing destructiveness and intolerableness of war (enabled by science) is a driving factor pushing toward demand for world control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as (1) among the compelling tendencies toward world control: 'The increasing destructiveness and intolerableness of war waged with the new powers of science.' It functions as an external pressure/criteria for urgency in federation arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fusion of the world's economic affairs
rubrics_metrics.description: The inevitable fusion of global economic affairs into one system, requiring some common control of currency and safe, uninterrupted global communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wells lists (2) 'the inevitable fusion of the world's economic affairs' leading to demands for common currency control, imports/exports freedom, and secure communications—used as a practical justification for world political authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global public health controls due to mobility
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of increasing mobility of peoples, there is a necessity for 'effectual controls of health everywhere.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as (3) among the movers toward world control; used as a criterion to justify supranational coordination of public health measures and policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equalization of labour conditions and minimum standards
rubrics_metrics.description: An urgent need for some equalization of labour conditions and a minimum standard of life worldwide, which implies establishing some minimum standard of education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item (4) in the list of pressures toward world control. Wells explicitly ties labour equalization to the corollary of universal minimum education, making social and educational standards part of the institutional requirements for a world state.

rubrics_metrics.name: World control of the air-ways
rubrics_metrics.description: The impossibility of developing the benefits of flying without a world control of the air-ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as (5); Wells treats technical/transport realities (air travel) as concrete grounds for supranational regulatory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common world religion (simplified and universalized)
rubrics_metrics.description: The coming world state will be based upon a common world religion: simplified, universalized, not any specialized form but religion itself pure—principles like brotherhood, creative service, and self-forgetfulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wells's (i) asserts religion (stripped of corruptions and priestly entanglements) as a synthetic moral basis for world unity. He suggests religious emotion may reappear 'stripped and plain' and aid the moral cohesion necessary for a global polity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal, lifelong education organized at world scale
rubrics_metrics.description: A universal education organized on an unprecedented scale and penetration: the whole race (not only classes) will be educated, with education continuing throughout life and many adults participating as educators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wells's (ii) includes details: 'perhaps ten per cent. or more of the adult population will... be workers in the world's educational organization' and education will be continuous through life. Education is treated as both a mechanism and criterion for legitimizing democratic, responsive government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abolition of standing armies, navies, and class of unemployed
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be no armies, no navies, and no classes of unemployed people, wealthy or poor — i.e., elimination of organized military forces and rigid socio-economic classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wells's (iii) sets the absence of professional fighting forces and rigid class structures as a defining institutional attribute of the ideal world-state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Massive organized scientific research and record-keeping
rubrics_metrics.description: The world state's organization of scientific research and record will be vastly more powerful and systematic than present arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wells's (iv) compares future scientific organization to 'an ocean liner beside the dug-out canoe,' indicating scale, centralization, and systematic record as evaluative characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: A vast free literature of criticism and discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be a vast free literature of criticism and discussion—publicity, debate, and critical discourse sustained at world scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wells's (v) highlights freedom of critique and discussion as both an institutional feature and a metric of the intellectual health of the world community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratic political organization responsive to educated population
rubrics_metrics.description: The world's political organization will be democratic; government will be in immediate touch with and responsive to the general thought of the educated whole population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wells's (vi) uses responsiveness to the 'educated whole population' as a standard for democratic legitimacy and operational responsiveness in a world-state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic organization for the common good with private enterprise as servant
rubrics_metrics.description: Economic organization will be the exploitation of natural wealth and possibilities by the agents of the common government for the common good; private enterprise will be a useful, well-rewarded servant rather than a 'robber master.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wells's (vii) defines the relationship between public economic control and private enterprise as a normative criterion: the economy must serve common welfare, with private business subordinate to public aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robust electoral methods and currency safeguards (mechanical guarantees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two difficult but essential achievements are: reliable electoral methods and a currency safeguarded or proof against manipulations by dishonest actors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wells's (viii) frames these as matters of mechanism necessary for political and economic well-being, analogous to reliable machinery for soldiers and pilots—i.e., operational/technical standards for institutional stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social justice ensuring health, education, and rough equality of opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: A federation of humanity must secure a sufficient measure of social justice to insure health, education, and a rough equality of opportunity for most children born into the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In §4 Wells links such social justice to massive increases in human productive energy and cultural achievement; this is both a moral standard and a pragmatic benchmark for judging the success of any proposed world arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of drudgery through mechanization and redistribution of work
rubrics_metrics.description: In a just world-state, drudgery will be largely eliminated: machines will do general drudge-work and any unavoidable drudgery will be done temporarily as service rather than a life-long degradation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wells argues this redistribution of work and harnessing of machines is an outcome criterion for improved human life and a sign that social/economic structures are functioning well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release and cultivation of latent human capacity via universal education
rubrics_metrics.description: Universal education and social justice will 'fish for capacity with the fine net of universal education,' yielding many more able scientists, artists, and investigators than previously realized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wells uses historical inference (lost potential due to poverty and war) to make this both an expected benefit and a metric: the extent to which society uncovers latent talent measures the success of reforms.
